51466908.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to SARS-CoV-2 Spike trimer protein by SPR analysis
51466908.references_previous: Reference [42] not found in bibliography. Reference [43] not found in bibliography.

original_paragraph.Materials and Methods - Surface plasmon: Compound UA-18 or UA-30 was fixed on the chip by photo-crosslinking, then recombinant SARS-CoV-2 S-trimer protein (DRA 47, Novoprotein Inc. Shanghai) at indicated concentrations was injected sequentially into the chamber in buffer PBST (0.1% Tween 20, pH 7.4). The interaction of S-trimer with UA-18 or UA-30 fixed was detected by PlexArrayTM HT SPRI (Seattle, US). The reaction temperature was controlled at 4 °C, binding time was 600 s, dissociation time was 360 s, flow rate was 0.5 μL/s. The chip was regenerated with Glycine Hydrochloride (pH 2.0). The data of interaction signals was retrieved and analyzed with PlexeraDE software [42,43].
original_paragraph.Figure 2 caption: Fig. 2. (A) Chemical structures of UA-18. (B) Dose-response curve for UA-18 in the antiviral assay against pSARS-CoV-2 and VSV-G infection on 293T-ACE2 cells. (C) Validation on the antiviral activity of UA-18 against authentic SARS-CoV-2 in Vero-E6 cells. (D) SPR analysis of the interaction between UA-18 with SARS-CoV-2 S-trimer.
original_paragraph.Figure 2D sensorgram data: Concentration of U-18 (μM): 2, 4, 8, 16, 32. Binding Signal (RU) ranges from 0 to 2000. K_D = 13.9 μM.
original_paragraph.Figure 5 caption: Fig. 5. (A) SPR analysis of the interaction between UA-30 with SARS-CoV-2 S-trimer. (B) The binding of SARS-CoV-2 S protein and ACE2 (Anti-Flag) in the presence or absence of UA-30 (40 μM) were detected by Co-IP assays. IgG was included as a negative control. (C) The dose-dependent inhibitory effect of UA-30 on SARS-CoV-2 S mediated cell-cell fusion.
original_paragraph.Figure 5A sensorgram data: Concentrations: 200 nM, 400 nM, 800 nM, 1600 nM, 3200 nM. Binding Signal (RU) ranges from 0 to 1600. K_D = 0.78 μM.
original_paragraph.Results section - SPR analysis of UA-30: Having confirmed these structure requirements of these UA saponins for maintaining high antiviral activity, we then designed experiments to identify the potential target. Consistent with the result of UA-18, a high affinity (K_D = 0.78 μM) was also observed between the lead UA-30 and the SARS-CoV-2 S protein based on an SPR assay (Fig. 5A), suggesting that the antiviral effect of UA-30 against SARS-CoV-2 infection derives from inhibition of viral entry into host cells by targeting the S protein.
